title: Henry Kolbeck and Olga de Visser's symbol message for Joe Bolner, San Antonio, seized at Laredo, February 1917 (BI case OG 2889): located with a key strip, not deciphered

documents.shelfmark: NARA RG 65, Bureau of Investigation, Old German Files (M1085), case OG 2889 (Olga Visser), roll 302 frames 39 and 58 (two photostats of one sheet); key strip on frames 42 and 59
documents.date: Feb 1917 (the carriers were detained at Laredo on 14 Feb 1917)

plaintext.source: The Bureau of Investigation read the note in 1917: E. E. Swift's reports in OG 3410 (M1085 roll 308, naId 369510329) quote the word 'avantaceran' (for abastecerán, 'will supply') from 'your copy of the note'; nothing else of its content is given (the 'men and guns' passage of 2 April 1917 concerns a different, planned credential letter). The full plaintext was not located; it may be in MID 9140-103 / 4131-44 (not digitised).

transcription.notes: Not transcribed. Seven lines of letter-like signs (some dotted) with short dashes inside the lines, plus a signature line; about 170-200 signs by eye (estimate, not counted). The frames are about 1000x1300 pixels and no larger copy was found.

system.summary: Handwritten symbol script of letter-like signs, some with dots above, short dashes inside the lines; a key strip in the same file pairs Latin letters (LL in its own cell) with signs, which suggests simple substitution over a Spanish alphabet, not tested.

diacritics.note: dots above some signs; function unknown

system.sibling_key: Key strip in OG 2889 (roll 302 frames 42 and 59); legible at the right end: j[?] C-shape with dot, K Λ, L †, LL ⊓ with tick, M[?]/Ñ[?] unclear, v[?] ✓[?] (lower row; the V may be the letter, not the sign). The strip may be a Bureau copy, and Franz Visser said Olga's key was used in the Vissers' own correspondence. Not shown to be this message's key; not applied.
system.notes: Kolbeck confessed in 1917 that he wrote the document himself in Laredo jail 'from a key he had originated in Mexico' (OG 3410). The message and the key strip share only some signs (†/T, 9, X, perhaps ✓).

prior_solution.where: Bureau of Investigation 1917: Swift's reports in OG 3410 (M1085 roll 308, naId 369510329) show the note was read in Spanish and quote one word; full plaintext not located (possibly MID 9140-103 / 4131-44, RG 165, not digitised). No printed treatment found by one web search; Tuchman and Boghardt not checked.

solution.what: From the DOJ alien enemy card 'VISSER, Olga' (naId 296747364) to Bureau of Investigation case OG 2889 (M1085 rolls 301-302; cover card roll 302 frame 40) and the companion case OG 3410 (Kolbeck, roll 308 frames 1988-2067).

Message found as two photostats of one sheet (roll 302 frames 39 and 58) and a key strip as two photostats (frames 42 and 59). Single frames downloaded a second time independently: same sizes as the images in the roll PDF; no higher resolution available.

Message and key strip examined on the frames: seven lines of letter-like signs with dashes and a signature line; on the key strip only the right end reads with some confidence (j[?], K, L, LL, M[?]/Ñ[?], v[?]). No sign-by-sign transcription made.

Bureau reports read in OCR (OG 2889, OG 3410, OG 2864): detention at Laredo on 14 Feb 1917; claimed sender Horotwischka of the Austro-Hungarian Legation; Kolbeck's confession that he wrote the document himself and the May 1917 charge; the Bureau's 1917 reading in Spanish ('avantaceran' = abastecerán; no other content given); the May 1917 complaint under section 37 of the Penal Code; a Bureau copy of the key made in April 1917.
Crib 'avasteceran' (pattern a?a???e?e?an) tried on the message by eye.

Independent recheck: frames re-downloaded and compared, page attribution confirmed, confession re-fetched from naId 369510329; corrected the first finding of 'no contemporary decode' to a 1917 reading in Spanish whose text is not located.
Web search (Olga Visser, Kolbeck, Laredo, code): no printed treatment found. Tuchman and Boghardt not checked.

outcome.method_basis: The message and a key strip were located as photostats in BI case OG 2889; no transcription or decryption was made, and the strip is not shown to be this message's key.

outcome.notes: Contributed by WAINUT (catalogue 698). Corrections: language Spanish, not German; carriers Henry Kolbeck and Olga de Visser (cousins); claimed sender the Legation secretary Hugo Horotwischka, not the minister; Kolbeck confessed he wrote it himself. Authenticity is open.
